items.item_text: Marriage and Family Therapist License or Licensed Clinical Social Worker.
CPR/BLS, Basic First Aid Certificate from American Red Cross or American Heart Association, must be updated as required

Bachelor’s degree in Child Development, Early Childhood Education, Human Development, Family Consumer Science, Sociology, Psychology, Social Sciences, Social Work, or related field, or equivalent working experience
Master’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, Marriage and Family Therapy, or related Mental health field
2 years of experience in a public or private organization, or community development agency providing direct delivery of services to clients.
2 years’ experience working directly with 0-5 children in a teaching position, families, and staff in an early care and education setting.

Under the general direction of the Health Nutrition Services Manager, the EHS Mental Health Coordinator is responsible for coordinating and implementing comprehensive mental health services for children, families, and pregnant women enrolled in the Early Head Start and Head Start programs. This position provides behavioral health assessments, counseling services, referrals, case management, and consultation to support children's social-emotional development and overall well-being. The EHS Mental Health Coordinator collaborates with families, staff, mental health consultants, and community partners to ensure timely access to services, monitors and analyzes mental health and developmental data, provides training and technical assistance to staff and parents, and supports compliance with Head Start Performance Standards and program requirements. This role plays a critical part in promoting positive child outcomes, strengthening family well-being, and ensuring the delivery of high-quality, culturally responsive mental health services.
Work Location(s): East San Fernando Valley- including but not limited to Arleta, Pacoima, Sylmar, Lake View Terrace, etc.
This is a limited position that may convert to career.
Understanding and use of the principles and practices of the ECE field, including reflective practice, dual language learning, and Practice-Based Coaching

Communicate effectively with staff and develop positive work relationships. Works collaboratively as a team player with her/his staff, clients (children and parents) and other professionals in the program/agency.

Per funding agency requirements, all Early Head Start staff must complete background checks prior to hire and at least every five years that includes, sex offender registry check, State or FBI criminal history check, including fingerprint check, child abuse registry check
Must meet state health requirements that include passing a physical examination as condition of employment, providing verification of COVID-19 vaccine, TB Clearance, and up to date with immunization.

Ability to communicate effectively with families, Early Head Start staff, community resource agencies, consultants and volunteers to support families in locating and accessing appropriate community services as needed.
Fluency and proficiency in English, Excellent written and oral communication skills, detail oriented. Bilingual in English and Spanish is preferred
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite; including Excel. Must be able to type at least 30 words per minute.
Knowledge of California Infant & Toddlers and Preschool Learning Foundations and Frameworks (Pre-K or Infant/Toddler as appropriate), Ages and Stages Questionnaire.
Ability to conduct onsite staff and/ or parent training when needed.
Knowledge in adult learning principles
Ability to provide education, training opportunities, and promote positive relationship building for all enrolled pregnant women, families and their infants and toddlers.
Sound organizational and time management skills to manage high and varied activity levels. Ability to organize and prioritize

Required Physical Abilities: Ability to carry children, up to 40 pounds, during each workday when necessary. Ability to engage in frequent bending, reaching, twisting and engage in moderate to frequent kneeling, crawling, and stooping while observing, or performing classroom activities. Ability to engage in frequent writing, typing on keyboards, and handling small objects (e.g. arts and crafts for children). Ability to sit or stand for prolonged periods of time that may exceed an hour at a time. This includes sitting on the floor for extended periods (e.g. while engaging in child development activities during home visits, classroom, and socialization sessions).
